correctness.rationale: The length-four predicate is tested exactly by edges of a 27-state three-letter overlap matrix. Closed walks are in bijection with indexed periodic words, even for periods one to three. Exact integer Newton identities reproduce all 27 coefficients of the factorization, and an independent direct enumeration reproduces the first eleven word counts. Formal determinant expansion and Möbius/Burnside inversion prove the all-length claims.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The ordinary square-free restriction is neither equal to nor stronger than root-two Abelian avoidance: ordinary squares of length two are prohibited only by the former, while anagrammatic nonordinary length-four squares are prohibited only by the latter. Avoiding all k-Abelian squares is another inequivalent problem. A known linear boundary recurrence gives one quartic factor but not the periodic-word trace or the additional factors.

value.rationale: Exact periodic and primitive-necklace counts for every length of a natural ternary fixed-root Abelian-square constraint provide a complete nontrivial constrained-system census. Cyclic closure contributes the explicit cubic and septic corrections absent from open-boundary recurrence, so this is not a routine substitution into that earlier formula. The case gives useful exact baseline for ternary periodic repetition-avoidance and code design without asserting broader applications.
